newsitem.title: USA: Genus to cut work force, take charge.
newsitem.headline: Genus to cut work force, take charge.

text.p: Genus Inc., a maker of equipment used in the fabrication of semiconductors, said Tuesday it plans to trim its staff by 39 workers or 11 percent of the company's permanent employees worldwide.

The Sunnyvale, Calif.-based company said it expects to take a restructuring charge of $3 million to $4 million, or 18 cents to 24 cents a share after-tax, during the third quarter to cover severance costs and other related charges.
"This work force reduction helps match company expenses with current economic realities resulting from the semiconductor industry downturn," said William Elder, Genus chairman and chief executive.
The company said it also plans cuts in discretionary spending and will continue to closely manage other operating expenses to further control costs.
Genus develops, manufactures, markets and services advanced thin film deposition equipment used to make advanced semiconductor devices.
Its stock fell 50 cents to $5.875 on Nasdaq at mid-morning.
